questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could get into the country. China was still closed down so Taiwan was the next best thing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is always a bit stressful to go to another country, but I think they made it easier with the information sheet they made.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did get a buddy from the university we could write with and could help us, but I never heard from mine so that was quite unlucky. Also there was a assistant that should had helped exchange students but that person changed 3 times while we were there and you never got a response back if you wrote an email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They had one you could apply for when you applied for the school. I was lucky and got into that one. (prince house).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: They had one kitchen, but it was dirty so I did not use it at all.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Maybe getting used to eat 2-3 out a day if you do not like the kitchen at your dorm. But it is very cheap to eat at the school so it was not that bad.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: So you were told before coming to the country about the registration and what documents you should have with you. On the day, you bring all of them and then you go around to the tables were you one after one, give the document you need. At the last table you will get your student ID. Pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As I told before there was one person, but she changed 3 times, so not very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: So this was an interesting process. You had the first two weeks to try out the classes you were interested in. I was lucky to get the classes that I wanted and that is not always the case.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be fast to get the registration code for the classes you really want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You could choose between 1, 2, and 3 credit courses. The 3 credit courses were the most workload. I had most of my courses 2 credit and 1 that were 3 credit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite good. Most of the professors were good and sweet.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Exploring Taiwan: Women and Taiwanese Society, General Chinese, Enhancing Chinese, Seminar on Asian Democratization, Exploring Taiwan: Natural Environment and resources, What really bugs you.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chinese if you want to order and talk with locals. Women and Taiwanese Society were fascinating also.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Books, i did not really think about that i had to buy that. Electricity for your room, that is not in your housing free every month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Electricity cost.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get into everything, a basketball club, Chinese club, handcraft club, cooking club, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chinese club is very interesting. You go and trips and can try calligraphy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to get local friends and go with them to celebrate the holidays with they family.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For be it was fine, because I had already been to china before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the clubs, be open and be patient.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How long they study for. They study to so late of night and still get up early in the morning for they classes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: how friendly and open they are to help you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to have fun and make friends even though the university workload can be challenging sometimes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a group with other exchange students because it was very helpful to have other that is in the same both as you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload from the school. But it it also the best school in Taiwan

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it! Its the best thing I ever did.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
